2609.19965.title: Before the Arrest: Benchmarking LLMs on Criminal Profiling from Incomplete Evidence
2609.19965.paper_summary: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to legal and criminal justice tasks, yet existing work focuses almost exclusively on post-arrest scenarios where the suspect's identity is already known, leaving the critical pre-arrest challenge of inferring suspect characteristics from incomplete evidence largely unexplored. To fill this gap, we introduce the Profiling, Investigation, and Judgment (PIJ), comprising 2,500 real homicide cases from five countries. PIJ evaluates LLMs across three tasks that span the entire criminal investigation pipeline: criminal profiling, which requires abductive reasoning to infer suspect attributes from fragmentary scene evidence, crime process reconstruction, which tests structured information extraction, and sentence prediction, which demands legal deductive reasoning. We evaluate 9 powerful LLMs and find that performance degrades systematically as tasks shift from explicit fact extraction to implicit reasoning over unknown suspect profiles. Categories requiring inferential reasoning, such as motivation and victim-offender relationships, remain the primary bottlenecks. Further analysis reveals substantial gaps between LLMs and human experts, along with pervasive biases in gender, age, and motive attribution. Our findings indicate that pre-arrest inference from incomplete evidence remains an open challenge.
2609.19965.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLMs）越來越多地應用於法律和刑事司法任務，但現有的研究幾乎完全專注於逮捕後的情境，這些情境中嫌疑人的身份已經確定，從而使得從不完整證據中推斷嫌疑人特徵的關鍵逮捕前挑戰大多未被探索。為了填補這一空白，我們引入了剖析、調查和判斷（PIJ），該模型包含來自五個國家的2,500個真實謀殺案件。PIJ在整個刑事調查流程中評估LLMs的三個任務：刑事剖析，這需要推理從片段現場證據中推斷嫌疑人屬性；犯罪過程重建，這測試結構化信息提取；以及判決預測，這要求法律推理。我們評估了9個強大的LLMs，發現隨著任務從明確的事實提取轉向對未知嫌疑人檔案的隱含推理，性能系統性下降。需要推理的類別，例如動機和受害者-犯罪者關係，仍然是主要瓶頸。進一步分析顯示LLMs與人類專家之間存在顯著差距，以及在性別、年齡和動機歸因方面普遍存在偏見。我們的研究結果表明，從不完整證據中進行逮捕前推理仍然是一個未解的挑戰。
